findings.claim: Digital Retina history contains materially different measurement generations that must not be collapsed into one accuracy number: a May-20 working-paper protocol reports 82.4% held-out phrase coverage over 47 images/1196 phrases at tau=0.22 with a 68.8% realistic-FPR-corrected lower bound; a May-26 Tier-3 strict-text audit reports 35.3% on a 12-image hard set and 47.5% on a 10-image easy set; a June-9 benchmark after targeted phrase-emission optimization reports 87.1% strict text on the tuned 12-image hard set and 70.0% strict text on an independent 32-image/681-phrase Freshset.
findings.implication: Preserve metric/protocol/version identity with every result. Current acceptance should not quote a single historical Retina accuracy without binding dataset, threshold, match rule, dictionary state and tuning ancestry.

findings.claim: The June-9 benchmark exposes strong threshold sensitivity for CLIP-lenient coverage on the hard set: 1.4% at 0.30, 13.6% at 0.26, 34.1% at 0.24, 66.3% at 0.22, 94.6% at 0.20 and 99.3% at 0.18. The same report explicitly identifies strict Freshset text coverage of 70.0% as the more conservative generalization estimate.
findings.implication: Harness must freeze threshold/match semantics and report strict textual/structured semantic utility separately from weak-signal encoder coverage. Historical 92-95% CLIP-lenient values are diagnostic, not interchangeable with downstream usable text correctness.

findings.claim: The Tier-3 audit records concrete failure families: YOLO's 80-class ceiling and false detections on art/AI imagery, CLIP vocabulary gaps, OCR failure on stylized/painted text, missing compositional binding and color/detail gaps. Region-BLIP improved some cases but also produced a harmful hallucinated interpretation on Kandinsky, showing that adding a perceptual stage can reduce semantic reliability.
findings.implication: Digital Retina acceptance needs adversarial art/AI/OCR/compositional-binding cases, calibrated uncertainty and per-stage provenance so a stronger-looking extra stage cannot silently override or amplify false evidence.

findings.claim: The extracted Drive tree exposes an implementation/evaluation lineage with deploy, api, frontend, eval, retina, tests, tools and a separate digital-retina-e2e tree. The historical project describes a 16-stage DAG and structured output surfaces rather than a single opaque caption model.
findings.implication: Reuse stage-level fixtures, eval corpora and provenance boundaries where source files validate them, but project outputs crossing the cognitive boundary must be converted to the current Clay-typed VisualPercept contract rather than preserved as untyped caption truth.

findings.claim: The Drive LCME benchmark corroborates low-latency local retrieval and the pre-fix scoring failure already known from Project-Frankenstein, but adds two useful long-horizon oracles: contradiction handling succeeds only 7/10 because old facts are not explicitly invalidated, and after a 200-turn conversation early-fact retrieval falls to P@1=0.750, P@5=0.875, MRR=0.792. The primary head-to-head quality benchmark itself used only 30 memory items and 20 labeled queries, so its near-perfect P@5 should not be treated as broad proof.
findings.implication: Add temporal contradiction/invalidation and long-noise retention tests to ClayGraph/UnifiedDB. Preserve LCME as a differential baseline, not an authoritative target.

findings.claim: Drive contains concrete LoRA adapter artifacts rather than only training notes. One visible adapter is 53,713,920 bytes and its config identifies base huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.5-4B-abliterated, PEFT LoRA r=32, alpha=64, dropout=0.1, targeting q/k/v/o/gate/up/down projections. A v25_final folder contains a separate 169,903,320-byte adapter artifact. The available v25 model card is boilerplate and does not document training data, evaluation, license, hardware or results.
findings.implication: Register these as historical model lineage/checkpoint assets and hash them if raw access permits. Do not infer model quality or current suitability from existence alone; final acceptance requires exact base+adapter+training/eval hashes and held-out evidence.

findings.claim: The frozen Drive v7 concept index covers 655 documents and 3762 relations but explicitly excludes complete code/database/model/binary asset enumeration. The newly traversed Retina, LCME and adapter trees demonstrate why the concept index cannot serve as the whole-Drive Level-0 denominator.
findings.implication: Whole-Drive PASS requires recursive asset-class inventory, hash/dedup and explicit semantic-vs-nonsemantic classification in addition to the concept/text submanifest.
